name: Trans Lifeline
summary: Peer support hotline run by and for trans people experiencing crisis or needing emotional support.

sections.title: About Trans Lifeline
sections.text: Trans Lifeline is a grassroots peer support hotline run by and for transgender people. Founded in 2014, it is the only trans-led crisis hotline in the United States and Canada. All operators are transgender and understand the unique challenges facing the trans community. Trans Lifeline operates on a consent-based model that prioritizes caller autonomy and does not engage in non-consensual active rescue practices.

sections.title: Who Should Call
sections.text: Trans Lifeline serves transgender and questioning individuals of any age experiencing emotional crisis, suicidal thoughts, or simply needing support from someone who understands. Common reasons to call include navigating transition, dealing with family rejection, experiencing discrimination or harassment, feeling isolated, processing complex emotions about gender identity, or needing help accessing trans-specific resources.

sections.title: How to Contact Trans Lifeline
sections.text: Call 1-877-565-8860 (US) or 1-877-330-6366 (Canada). The hotline is available 24/7, though staffing levels vary. Wait times may be longer during overnight hours. All calls are answered by transgender peer support operators. The service is free and confidential. Trans Lifeline does not trace calls or contact emergency services without explicit consent.

sections.title: Trans Lifeline Microgrants
sections.text: Trans Lifeline offers microgrants to help trans people access name changes, updated identity documents, and other transition-related needs. The organization has distributed thousands of grants to help trans people obtain legal documents that match their gender identity. These grants help reduce barriers to accessing affirming documents, employment, and housing.

sections.title: Support for Family and Friends
sections.text: Trans Lifeline also provides support for family members, friends, and allies of transgender people who want to better understand and support their loved ones. Operators can provide resources, answer questions, and offer guidance on how to be supportive. The organization's website includes educational materials about transgender experiences and how to be an ally.
